question: Why must a chest drainage system always be placed lower than the patient's chest?

options.A: To make it easier for the patient to walk around the unit
options.B: To ensure the water seal chamber bubbles continuously
options.C: To use gravity to keep fluid draining away from the pleural cavity
options.D: To prevent the suction regulator from breaking

explanation: You nailed it! Gravity is our helper here; keeping the canister low ensures fluid drains out of the chest and doesn't flow back in.

question: What is a top priority at the bedside for a patient struggling with swallowing due to lower cranial nerve trouble?

options.A: Performing passive range of motion exercises on all extremities
options.B: Applying warm compresses to the forehead to relieve headache
options.C: Keeping mechanical suction equipment ready at the bedside
options.D: Encouraging a high-fiber diet to prevent constipation

explanation: You got this! Patients with trouble swallowing can easily choke or aspirate, so having suction ready keeps them safe.

question: What should you do if you are unsure about a drug dosage calculation?

options.A: Give half the amount to be safe and wait for complaints
options.B: Have a second nurse independently calculate and verify the dose
options.C: Call the hospital security team to supervise the injection
options.D: Guess the amount based on the patient's physical size

explanation: Two brains are better than one! Getting an independent double-check from a colleague is a gold standard for catching math errors before they reach the patient.

question: What is the final outcome of spermatogenesis in human males?

options.A: One large ovum and three polar bodies
options.B: Two identical diploid zygotes
options.C: Four functional spermatozoa
options.D: One functional sperm and three polar bodies

explanation: Great job! Unlike egg formation which makes just one large egg, spermatogenesis neatly divides to produce four healthy, ready-to-go sperm cells.

question: What is a frequent risk when people try to self-medicate ongoing, untreated anxiety?

options.A: Substance abuse and dependence
options.B: Sudden permanent loss of vision
options.C: Drastic and rapid skeletal bone growth
options.D: Complete immunity to bacterial infections

explanation: Spot on. Many turn to alcohol or drugs to numb their anxious feelings, which often leads into a struggle with substance dependence.

question: According to standard infection control rules, how often should primary IV tubing be changed?

options.A: 24 to 36 hours
options.B: Only until the bag empties
options.C: 72 to 96 hours
options.D: Every 7 days exactly

explanation: Spot on! Standard primary lines are generally swapped out every 3 to 4 days (72 to 96 hours) to keep bacteria from building up.

question: What simple tool do nurses use at local health clinics to catch early signs of poor growth in infants?

options.A: Magnetic resonance imaging scanners
options.B: Weight growth monitoring charts
options.C: Advanced blood pressure monitors
options.D: Surgical scalpels and forceps

explanation: Regular weighing and plotting on growth charts help nurses spot faltering nutrition before severe malnutrition sets in. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h3)

question: What are the three main components that drive normal labor?

options.A: Placenta, position, and pain
options.B: Pulse, pressure, and pelvis
options.C: Perineum, protein, and pushing
options.D: Passenger, passage, and power

explanation: Labor progress depends entirely on the baby (passenger), the birth canal (passage), and uterine contractions (power). [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h2)

question: What is a common myth people believe about using digital tools in nursing practice?

options.A: People believe computers can completely replace all doctors and nurses.
options.B: People think digital materials can only be used by illiterate community members.
options.C: People assume mobile phones do not require any battery power to operate.
options.D: People believe digital tools completely replace traditional face-to-face nursing contact.

explanation: Digital tools are awesome helpers, but they can never replace the warmth and trust of real human touch and face-to-face nursing care.

question: Which of the following is a common logistical barrier to immunization in rural areas?

options.A: Too many nurses working in primary health centers
options.B: Poor road networks and long geographical distances
options.C: An overabundance of vaccine supplies
options.D: Excessive availability of cold storage boxes

explanation: Bad roads and remote locations make it very hard for health workers to transport vaccines and for families to reach clinics. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h2)

question: A nurse teaches mothers why immunization prevents killer childhood diseases. Which learning domain is this mainly addressing?

options.A: Cognitive domain
options.B: Affective domain
options.C: Psychomotor domain
options.D: Financial domain

explanation: Teaching the reasons behind disease prevention and building mental understanding targets the cognitive domain of knowledge.

question: Where should community-based mental health interventions ideally take place to be most effective?

options.A: Exclusively inside high-security psychiatric hospital wards
options.B: In familiar local spaces like schools, markets, and places of worship
options.C: Only through remote internet video calls managed by government agencies
options.D: Strictly inside university research laboratories

explanation: Taking mental health services into familiar community settings reduces stigma and makes care much easier for residents to access. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h6)

question: A patient experiences severe dehydration. What immediate effect does this have on body function?

options.A: Sudden increase in muscle mass and bone density
options.B: Immediate conversion of fats into stored carbohydrates
options.C: Disruption of metabolic processes and electrolyte balance
options.D: Rapid overproduction of digestive enzymes in the gut

explanation: Without enough water, blood volume drops, electrolytes concentrate abnormally, and cellular chemical reactions slow down or fail. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h4)

question: Which ventilator mode gives a full machine breath whenever the patient tries to breathe, plus a backup rate just in case?

options.A: Assist-Control
options.B: Spontaneous breathing
options.C: Control Mode
options.D: SIMV

explanation: In Assist-Control mode, the machine is right there helping. Every time the patient initiates a breath, the ventilator steps in to deliver a full breath, and a backup rate ensures they never miss one.

question: Which specific vitamin needs a special helper protein called 'intrinsic factor' from the stomach to be absorbed properly?

options.A: Folic acid
options.B: Vitamin B12
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: Intrinsic factor is like a VIP escort for Vitamin B12! It teams up in the stomach to protect the vitamin until they reach the lower part of the small intestine for absorption.

question: What happens when a patient lacks essential haematinics?

options.A: Red blood cell production is impaired
options.B: White blood cells multiply uncontrollably
options.C: Platelets aggregate too quickly in vessels
options.D: The heart slows down its pumping rate

explanation: Without raw materials like iron, the bone marrow simply doesn't have what it needs to pump out enough red blood cells. Great job connecting the dots!

question: Which waste products are eliminated from the body through sweat?

options.A: Excess carbon dioxide and oxygen
options.B: Red blood cells and blood platelets
options.C: Undigested food particles and fiber
options.D: Salt, water, and small amounts of urea

explanation: Sweat contains mostly water and salt, along with minor metabolic waste products like urea. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the main focus of palliative care in a residential care home?

options.A: Discharging residents to an acute hospital ward immediately
options.B: Aggressive medical interventions to cure terminal chronic illnesses
options.C: Providing comfort, pain management, and dignity during end-of-life
options.D: Restricting family visits to maintain strict facility quiet hours

explanation: Brilliant! Palliative care is all about comforting patients, easing pain, and giving them dignity when curing is no longer possible.

question: Which of these is NOT a standard rule when picking essential medicines?

options.A: Proven clinical effectiveness in human trials
options.B: Affordability for the target patient population
options.C: Safety compared to other choices
options.D: The aesthetic appeal of the product packaging

explanation: Correct! A pretty wrapper doesn't make a drug safer or more effective for our patients.

question: What is a major effect of malnutrition in school children?

options.A: Impaired learning capacity and weakened immunity
options.B: Enhanced resistance to common viral infections
options.C: Rapid acceleration in physical height and bone density
options.D: Increased ability to focus for long hours

explanation: That's right! Without proper nutrients, the body and brain struggle, leading to poor concentration, tiredness, and frequent sickness.

question: Which two nutrients are most essential for building and maintaining strong bones?

options.A: Iron and vitamin B12
options.B: Potassium and sodium
options.C: Protein and vitamin C
options.D: Calcium and vitamin D

explanation: Calcium builds bone structure, and vitamin D is necessary for the body to absorb that calcium properly. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h5)

question: What is the main benefit of knowing basic nutrition terms at the bedside?

options.A: Calculating precise hospital food budgets
options.B: Diagnosing rare genetic disorders
options.C: Prescribing tube feeding formulas independently
options.D: Spotting early signs of nutritional decline

explanation: Spotting trouble early lets you advocate for your patient before a minor nutrition issue turns into a major clinical problem. You've got this!

question: Which of these statements is true regarding passive immunity?

options.A: It provides immediate but temporary protection
options.B: It relies entirely on the patient's bone marrow activity
options.C: It takes several weeks before any antibodies appear
options.D: It creates long-lasting immunological memory cells

explanation: Passive immunity is like borrowing an umbrella in the rain—you get instant protection from someone else's antibodies, but it wears off quickly because your body made no memory cells.

question: Where is the best spot to set up a temporary disaster field hospital?

options.A: Directly inside an unstable damaged building
options.B: In the deepest part of the flooded zone
options.C: As far away from the disaster victims as possible
options.D: On stable, accessible ground away from immediate hazards

explanation: Makes total sense! We want a safe, solid spot that ambulances and walking patients can easily reach without getting caught in secondary dangers.

question: What kind of authority does a nurse have when others listen to them purely because of their special clinical skills and advanced training?

options.A: Traditional authority
options.B: Charismatic authority
options.C: Formal authority
options.D: Expert authority

explanation: Brilliant! When respect and obedience come from your deep knowledge and specialized skills, that's your 'expert authority' shining through.

question: When is it legally and ethically okay to use physical restraints or seclusion on a ward?

options.A: When the ward is short-staffed and busy
options.B: If the patient refuses to participate in group therapy
options.C: Whenever the nursing shift changes in the morning
options.D: When the patient is an immediate danger to self or others

explanation: Restraints are an absolute last resort. We only use them to keep the patient and everyone around them safe from immediate physical harm.

question: Why is defining your research goal the most crucial first step when designing a checklist?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will agree to participate in the study
options.B: It eliminates the need for any literature review during the project
options.C: It determines the final statistical software the study will use
options.D: It guides which specific variables and items need to be included

explanation: When you know your exact goal, every single item you put on that checklist will directly serve your research purpose.

question: Which home change is most important for a patient who uses a wheelchair?

options.A: Removing all windows to improve ventilation
options.B: Widening doorways and installing access ramps
options.C: Replacing all tiled floors with thick carpets
options.D: Installing bright fluorescent lighting in every room

explanation: Wheelchair users need ramps to handle steps and widened doorways so they can move freely and safely from room to room.

question: Why is it important for a primary health nurse to understand local traditional health beliefs?

options.A: It proves that traditional practices are always superior to science
options.B: It allows the nurse to replace all modern medicine with herbs
options.C: It stops patients from ever visiting local herbalists
options.D: It helps build trust and improves cooperation with medical treatments

explanation: Respecting traditional views helps nurses bridge the gap between community practices and safe, evidence-based health care. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T12#GNS124_U5_T12_h5)

question: What is a very common cause of accidental needle-stick injuries during a busy shift?

options.A: Transporting sealed waste boxes
options.B: Attempting to recap used needles
options.C: Washing non-sterile kidney dishes
options.D: Checking intravenous infusion lines

explanation: Trying to put the cap back on a used needle with two hands is a recipe for a missed cap and a finger prick. Never recap!

question: Why do nurses need to know about crowd safety during mass gatherings?

options.A: Hospital administrators mandate that all nurses work at concerts and festivals.
options.B: Large crowds often produce sudden medical needs that can overwhelm local hospitals.
options.C: Crowd events are the only places nurses encounter infectious diseases.
options.D: Nurses are legally required to act as event security commanders.

explanation: When thousands of people gather, medical emergencies happen! Nurses play a key role in planning so local hospitals don't get completely overwhelmed.

question: How does close communication between nurses and family caregivers impact client care?

options.A: It ensures consistency between care practices at the center and at home
options.B: It prevents the nursing staff from making independent clinical choices
options.C: It creates unnecessary confusion and conflicting daily schedules
options.D: It allows the family to completely delegate all thinking to the staff

explanation: Sharing observations and strategies between home and the facility creates a unified approach that benefits the client's stability and comfort. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h7)

question: How do bacterial efflux pumps help germs beat drugs?

options.A: By blocking white blood cells from entering tissues
options.B: By dissolving the outer layer of human skin cells
options.C: By actively pushing the medication out of the cell
options.D: By creating new vitamins that feed the pathogen

explanation: Think of efflux pumps like tiny security guards that rapidly throw drug molecules right back out before they can harm the microbe!

question: Which condition means a patient must NEVER be given misoprostol?

options.A: Well-managed gestational diabetes
options.B: Mild iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: A history of high blood pressure
options.D: A confirmed ectopic pregnancy

explanation: Misoprostol cannot treat a pregnancy outside the uterus. Giving it would dangerously delay emergency surgery. Always check for this first!

question: Why does the internal urethral sphincter need to close tightly during emission?

options.A: To slow down the heart rate during arousal
options.B: To allow urine to mix freely with seminal fluid
options.C: To increase testosterone production in the testes
options.D: To prevent retrograde movement of semen into the bladder

explanation: Exactly! Closing that door ensures semen goes forward out of the penis instead of taking a wrong turn backward into the bladder.

question: How do in-text citations connect to your reference list at the end?

options.A: The reference list contains sources you read but did not cite
options.B: They use completely different formatting styles from each other
options.C: Every in-text citation must match a full entry in the reference list
options.D: In-text citations are only used if the reference list is missing

explanation: Think of them as best friends: if you mention a source in your paragraph, it must have its full home address in your reference list!

question: Who can show leadership in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Only the appointed director of nursing
options.B: Only nurses with over twenty years of experience
options.C: Any nurse guiding care and supervising colleagues
options.D: Hospital chief executive officers exclusively

explanation: You don't need a fancy title to be a leader! Leadership is about your actions and positive influence. Even as a junior or staff nurse, you lead every time you guide patient care or help a colleague.

question: You organize a support group for mothers managing sickle cell anemia across three different towns. What type of community have you formed?

options.A: A geographic community
options.B: A rural farming community
options.C: An urban slum settlement
options.D: A community of interest

explanation: Spot on! Even though they live in different towns, they are united by a common health experience, making them a classic community of interest.

question: Which airway maneuver is safest to use when a neck injury is suspected?

options.A: Neck-hyperextension method
options.B: Rapid lateral neck rotation
options.C: Jaw-thrust maneuver
options.D: Head-tilt/chin-lift maneuver

explanation: The jaw-thrust maneuver opens the airway without moving or bending the cervical spine, protecting the patient from further spinal cord damage. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h3)

question: Why is ethical data management particularly critical in nursing research?

options.A: Because it prevents frequency tables from having errors
options.B: Because computers cannot process named data without codes
options.C: Because nursing data involves sensitive personal health information
options.D: Because ethical clearance replaces the need for data cleaning

explanation: Healthcare records are deeply private, and nurses have an ethical duty to safeguard patient confidentiality throughout every step of data organization. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h8)

question: What is the easiest and most reliable way to track rapid fluid loss in a patient with diarrhoea?

options.A: Daily body weight measurements
options.B: Body temperature fluctuations
options.C: Changes in skin color on the face
options.D: Total number of hours slept per night

explanation: Weight drops fast when you lose body water. Hopping on the scale daily is one of the best ways to catch dangerous dehydration early.

question: A nurse takes time to explain a new diabetic diet to a confused patient and their family. What role is this nurse performing?

options.A: Radiologist
options.B: Laboratory technician
options.C: Facility director
options.D: Educator

explanation: Teaching patients and families how to manage their health and care for themselves at home is a core part of our educator role. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the main difference between a standard IV infusion and a blood transfusion?

options.A: Transfusions never require a special intravenous line
options.B: Infusions are always given faster than blood transfusions
options.C: Infusions can only use blood products while transfusions use plain water
options.D: Infusions deliver fluids or medications while transfusions replace blood components

explanation: You've got this! Regular IV fluids give water, salts, or drugs, while blood transfusions specifically replace parts of the blood like red cells or plasma. Simple and clear!

question: A 32-year-old woman who has always had painless periods suddenly develops severe, worsening cramps during every cycle over the last year. Which condition is she most likely experiencing?

options.A: Primary dysmenorrhoea
options.B: Secondary dysmenorrhoea
options.C: Normal ovulatory pain
options.D: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder

explanation: Onset of severe menstrual pain later in life, especially when it progressively worsens, is a classic sign of secondary dysmenorrhoea. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h3)

question: A patient develops a fungal mouth infection (oral thrush) after taking strong antibiotics. Why did this happen?

options.A: Antibiotics caused the patient's immune system to stop producing white blood cells
options.B: The medication directly stimulated the rapid growth of fungal spores in the throat
options.C: The antibiotics destroyed the protective normal bacteria that usually keep the fungus in check
options.D: The patient consumed contaminated food while taking the prescribed pills

explanation: Strong antibiotics are like a bomb in the gut and mouth—they wipe out the good bacteria that normally keep fungi like Candida under control, letting the fungus multiply unchecked.

question: What is the main purpose of a formal grievance procedure in a hospital?

options.A: To give management an easy excuse to fire disobedient nurses
options.B: To determine which staff members deserve annual promotion
options.C: To resolve staff complaints fairly without fear of victimization
options.D: To bypass national labour laws during salary negotiations

explanation: A grievance procedure is a safe, official channel where staff can voice complaints or resolve workplace issues without worrying that management will punish them for speaking up.

question: Why is teamwork with other professionals so important in gender-based violence cases?

options.A: Nurses lack the medical training to diagnose bruises
options.B: Legal authorities handle all counseling and housing needs directly
options.C: Hospital policies prohibit nurses from talking to victims alone
options.D: Complex social, legal, and safety needs require specialized community support

explanation: You've nailed it! No single nurse can do it all. Working with social workers, legal aid, and shelters is key to helping a survivor heal.

question: Where can healthcare workers quickly find safety details, hazard warnings, and emergency steps for a specific chemical?

options.A: Hospital dietary meal manual
options.B: Safety Data Sheet (SDS)
options.C: General nursing care textbook
options.D: Daily facility staffing schedule

explanation: Every hospital department has them. The Safety Data Sheet (SDS) is your best friend for looking up how to safely handle a chemical and what to do if an accident happens.

question: Which set of lab tests is primarily ordered to check how well the thyroid gland is working?

options.A: Serum sodium and potassium levels
options.B: Morning cortisol and ACTH levels
options.C: Fasting glucose and HbA1c levels
options.D: TSH, T3, and T4 levels

explanation: Spot on! Checking TSH (the boss hormone from the pituitary) along with T3 and T4 (the actual thyroid hormones) gives a complete picture of thyroid health.

question: Why do many traditional taboos give the best pieces of meat to adult males instead of children?

options.A: Cultural hierarchy assigns priority foods to providers and leaders
options.B: Adult males require more physical energy to farm and hunt
options.C: Children's digestive systems cannot process animal protein
options.D: Meat spoils faster when eaten by younger family members

explanation: Traditional power structures often dictate that heads of households and male breadwinners receive the most prized food items first.

question: Why are day care centres particularly vulnerable to infectious disease outbreaks?

options.A: Clients live permanently inside the building
options.B: Groups of vulnerable individuals gather in close contact
options.C: Staff members are not allowed to wash their hands
options.D: Sanitation guidelines forbid the use of soap and water

explanation: Gathering young children or frail adults in enclosed spaces makes it easy for germs to spread rapidly among them. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h4)

question: Which of these is a clear example of artificial active immunity?

options.A: Getting a polio vaccine at the primary health clinic
options.B: Drinking colostrum from a mother immediately after birth
options.C: Catching chickenpox from a classmate at school
options.D: Receiving snake antivenom after a bite on the farm

explanation: Spot on! Vaccines introduce harmless germ parts (antigens) so your body actively builds its own defense.

question: What is the job of intrinsic activity when a drug acts in the body?

options.A: It measures the weight of the active pharmaceutical ingredient.
options.B: It prevents the drug from entering the bloodstream.
options.C: It triggers a biological response after the drug binds.
options.D: It determines how fast the kidneys clear the medicine.

explanation: Once the drug locks onto its receptor, intrinsic activity is the spark that actually makes the cell change its behavior. Great job learning the basics!

question: What is formed at the very end of the clotting process to firmly seal a damaged blood vessel?

options.A: Soluble fibrinogen
options.B: Unbound platelets
options.C: Inactive thrombin
options.D: Stable fibrin mesh

explanation: At the finish line of the clotting cascade, fibrinogen turns into a strong, stable fibrin mesh that holds the blood clot firmly in place like a net.

question: Why do nurses check the ear canal with an otoscope after finishing an irrigation?

options.A: To check if the patient's hearing loss is permanent
options.B: To measure the exact length of the ear canal
options.C: To pump remaining air out of the middle ear space
options.D: To make sure the wax or object is actually gone

explanation: An otoscope check lets you double-check your work and confirm the ear canal is clean and the eardrum looks safe. Perfect finish!

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine restricts exposed healthy people
options.B: Quarantine is permanent, while isolation lasts for only a few hours
options.C: Isolation is for animals, while quarantine is strictly for human patients
options.D: Quarantine uses medications, while isolation only uses physical barriers

explanation: Easy way to remember: Isolation keeps already sick people away from others. Quarantine keeps healthy people who were exposed to a germ apart, just in case they develop symptoms later.

question: Why is psychological first aid provided by nurses so important after a disaster?

options.A: It helps traumatized survivors cope with immediate shock, grief, and emotional distress
options.B: It immediately repairs damaged physical infrastructure like roads and houses
options.C: It cures chronic physical diseases that existed before the disaster
options.D: It replaces the need for surgical operations in severe trauma cases

explanation: Brilliant! Disasters leave deep emotional scars. Psychological support helps survivors process the shock and start their healing journey.

question: What should be clearly recorded in the patient's register when a standing order is used?

options.A: The specific protocol used, assessment findings, and treatments given
options.B: The political affiliation of the patient receiving care
options.C: The personal home address of the facility's medical director
options.D: A detailed financial profit statement for the pharmacy unit

explanation: Proper documentation requires noting the exact protocol followed, clinical findings, and interventions administered for legal and continuity purposes. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h7)

question: Which of these is a major duty of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare?

options.A: Building commercial real estate for private citizens
options.B: Issuing traffic tickets in major cities
options.C: Collecting personal income taxes from workers
options.D: Formulating national health policies and setting clinical standards

explanation: You got it! The federal ministry sets the big-picture rules and clinical standards that guide healthcare practice all across Nigeria.

question: Which of these is a classic example of indirect transmission via a fomite?

options.A: Catching an infection after touching a contaminated door handle
options.B: Getting malaria from a mosquito bite
options.C: Contracting a sexually transmitted infection through direct contact
options.D: Inhaling large droplets expelled during a close-range sneeze

explanation: A 'fomite' is just a fancy word for any non-living object—like a door handle, phone, or pen—that carries germs from one person to another.

question: Why is it so tricky to spot an asymptomatic carrier during a disease outbreak?

options.A: Pathogens cannot be detected in their bodily fluids
options.B: They show no outward signs of illness but can still spread the pathogen to others
options.C: Their laboratory blood tests always return completely normal results
options.D: They refuse to answer questions about their daily activities

explanation: That's why outbreaks can be sneaky. These carriers feel completely fine and show zero symptoms, yet they can still pass the germs along to others without knowing it.

question: While local anesthesia is given during the procedure, what is a key thing for the nurse to watch out for?

options.A: Applying pressure dressings before the surgeon cuts the foreskin
options.B: Checking that the local anesthetic solution is heated to body temperature
options.C: Watching for signs of systemic toxicity like changes in breathing or alertness
options.D: Recording the exact time the patient falls into a deep sleep

explanation: You're doing great. If a local anesthetic gets absorbed too quickly into the bloodstream, it can cause reactions. Monitoring the baby's breathing and alertness keeps them safe.

question: Which of the following is considered a primary biological data source for disease confirmation?

options.A: Political speeches
options.B: Laboratory records
options.C: Newspaper reports
options.D: Market sales receipts

explanation: Laboratory test results provide the scientific proof needed to confirm the exact organism causing an illness. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which of these best describes 'disenfranchised grief'?

options.A: Loss that society does not openly acknowledge or validate
options.B: Grief caused exclusively by the loss of a physical body part
options.C: Sudden grief that disappears within a few hours of the event
options.D: Mourning that only occurs after a legal dispute over an estate

explanation: Well done! Disenfranchised grief happens when society doesn't give someone space or recognition to mourn openly. Think of it as a hidden or unsupported loss.

question: What is the main job of androgens (like testosterone) in the normal female body?

options.A: Stopping all activity in the anterior pituitary gland
options.B: Triggering immediate shedding of the uterine lining
options.C: Maintaining thick cervical mucus to block sperm entry
options.D: Supporting bone strength, libido, and serving as a precursor for estrogen

explanation: Even though they're often called 'male' hormones, women have them too! They keep your bones strong, fuel your energy and drive, and help build estrogen.

question: How should a washed diaphragm be stored after it dries?

options.A: In its designated storage case away from heat and sunlight
options.B: Wrapped tightly in a plastic bag inside the kitchen freezer
options.C: At the bottom of a handbag without any protective covering
options.D: Hanging openly on a bathroom wall hook exposed to light

explanation: Keeping it in its cool, dark storage case protects the material from heat and sunlight, helping it last a long time.

question: What does a directional hypothesis predict?

options.A: The specific direction of the relationship between variables
options.B: The exact cost of conducting the clinical study
options.C: That no relationship exists between the variables
options.D: The total number of patients needed for the sample

explanation: It points the way! Words like 'increase', 'decrease', 'higher', or 'lower' tell you which way the results are expected to go.

question: What is the main goal of doing a Spontaneous Breathing Trial (SBT)?

options.A: To measure the exact lung compliance and resistance parameters
options.B: To evaluate if a patient can tolerate breathing without ventilator support
options.C: To allow the patient to recover from heavy sedative medications
options.D: To clear thick mucus plugs from the lower airways before extubation

explanation: An SBT is like a test drive! We lower the machine's help to see if the patient's lungs and muscles are strong enough to handle breathing all on their own.

question: A patient who had a leg amputation complains of severe pain in the toes of the missing foot. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Tell the patient firmly that the foot is gone so it cannot hurt
options.B: Remove the surgical dressing immediately to look for infection
options.C: Acknowledge the pain and administer prescribed medication for phantom limb pain
options.D: Check the remaining leg for signs of a new injury

explanation: Phantom limb sensations and pain are very real neurological events that require validation and appropriate medical treatment. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h5)

question: A midwife spends extra time during an antenatal visit explaining birth spacing and handing out modern contraceptive supplies. Which nursing role does this best demonstrate?

options.A: Agricultural policy formulation
options.B: Financial auditing and taxation
options.C: Urban infrastructural planning
options.D: Policy execution and patient advocacy

explanation: By counseling patients and providing family planning supplies right there in the clinic, you are actively bringing national health policies to life and advocating for your patients!

question: When does the liver start producing ketone bodies?

options.A: When glucose is unavailable and fats are broken down for fuel
options.B: When the patient drinks excessive amounts of water
options.C: Right after eating a large meal high in simple sugars
options.D: During heavy weightlifting exercise using arm muscles

explanation: If glucose runs low, the body switches to burning fat for fuel, which creates ketone bodies as a backup energy source.

question: Why is getting an autoimmune disease diagnosed often a long and tricky journey?

options.A: Blood tests are completely unavailable for most autoimmune conditions
options.B: Early symptoms are vague, overlapping, and resemble many other common illnesses
options.C: Autoimmune markers change completely every single day
options.D: Patients rarely report their symptoms to healthcare providers early on

explanation: Early signs like tiredness and body aches look like everyday malaria or stress, making it tough for doctors to pin down right away.

question: What is the main goal of nursing research?

options.A: To increase the financial revenue of private health institutions
options.B: To replace traditional medical diagnoses with nursing diagnoses
options.C: To build a knowledge base that guides practice and improves patient outcomes
options.D: To reduce the administrative workload of hospital managers

explanation: Spot on! Nursing research is all about finding out what works best so we can give our patients the safest, highest quality care possible.

question: Why must nurses check for G6PD deficiency before giving a patient primaquine?

options.A: To prevent severe hemolytic anemia in vulnerable patients
options.B: To confirm the liver is strong enough to process the drug
options.C: To ensure the patient does not have a concurrent bacterial infection
options.D: To check if the patient is already immune to malaria

explanation: Safety first! Patients with G6PD deficiency lack the protection needed to keep their red blood cells stable against primaquine, which can trigger dangerous red blood cell breakdown (hemolysis).

question: Which of these is a basic shared need that brings a community together?

options.A: Employment in corporate technology firms
options.B: Membership in international political parties
options.C: Access to clean water and basic healthcare
options.D: Ownership of luxury motor vehicles

explanation: Things like clean water, food, and basic health services are everyday priorities that unite everyone.

question: A patient is admitted with bleeding oesophageal varices. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Performing a detailed swallow screening test
options.B: Monitoring vital signs and securing IV access
options.C: Encouraging gentle physical exercise daily
options.D: Teaching dietary changes to prevent acid reflux

explanation: Safety first! Active bleeding is an emergency. You must check their vital signs right away and get a drip running so you can replace lost fluids and keep them stable.

question: Why is proper sewage disposal so important for community health?

options.A: It completely eliminates all chemical pollutants from manufacturing plants
options.B: It provides essential mineral nutrients for local agricultural soil
options.C: It stops disease-causing germs from reaching drinking water sources
options.D: It lowers the overall temperature of surrounding urban neighborhoods

explanation: When we manage waste safely, we create a barrier that keeps harmful germs away from the water we drink and the places where we live. Great job protecting the public!

question: Why do older adults often need fewer total calories but still require plenty of vitamins and minerals?

options.A: They have a slower metabolism, but still need nutrients to protect bones and muscles
options.B: Their digestive systems completely stop absorbing all forms of dietary fat
options.C: Older adults naturally stop growing taller, so their cells no longer need any energy
options.D: They require fewer nutrients because their bodies are fully mature

explanation: As people age, their bodies burn less energy overall, but they still need a good mix of vitamins and minerals to keep bones strong and prevent muscle loss.

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important for patients managing celiac disease?

options.A: Mental stress directly converts into physical gluten proteins inside the gut.
options.B: Patients usually develop severe memory loss from carbohydrate withdrawal.
options.C: Strict dietary restriction and social isolation can create significant emotional distress.
options.D: Psychological counseling is the only proven cure for intestinal villous atrophy.

explanation: Living with a lifelong, rigid diet can feel isolating and stressful. Being a warm, supportive nurse makes all the difference for their mental well-being!

question: What does active immunization (like a vaccine) trigger the body to make?

options.A: Temporary foreign plasma proteins
options.B: Non-specific physical skin barriers
options.C: Immediate exogenous red blood cells
options.D: Its own antibodies and memory cells

explanation: Exactly! Vaccines train your body to do the heavy lifting by creating its own long-lasting antibodies and memory cells.

question: A patient post-abortion complains of sudden, sharp belly pain, and her abdomen feels very hard and stiff. What complication should come to mind?

options.A: Post-procedure anxiety
options.B: Mild urinary tract infection
options.C: Normal uterine cramping
options.D: Uterine perforation

explanation: You've got it! A rigid, painful belly is a red flag that the uterine wall may have been accidentally punctured.

question: Which patient will benefit most from a nebulizer instead of a standard inhaler?

options.A: An active athlete who needs a quick rescue puff before playing football
options.B: A severely breathless patient who struggles to coordinate breathing with an inhaler
options.C: A healthy adult who prefers taking their daily maintenance medication quickly
options.D: A patient who experiences dry mouth from using anticholinergic inhalers

explanation: Nebulizers turn liquid medicine into a cool mist that the patient can breathe in easily during normal breathing, making them perfect for someone in severe respiratory distress.

question: What is the main test used to diagnose structural heart valve problems?

options.A: Echocardiogram
options.B: Routine head CT scan
options.C: Standard skin biopsy
options.D: Abdominal ultrasound

explanation: An echo is an ultrasound of the heart! It lets doctors actually see the heart valves moving and check how well blood is flowing.

question: Which human sense is widely believed to be the very last to fade when someone is dying?

options.A: Taste
options.B: Hearing
options.C: Sight
options.D: Smell

explanation: Hearing stays active right to the end! That's why we always encourage families to keep talking, praying, and whispering sweet words to their loved one.

question: What is a major limitation of descriptive research designs?

options.A: They require complex laboratory machinery
options.B: They cannot use questionnaires or interviews
options.C: They are too expensive for ordinary nursing students
options.D: They cannot prove cause-and-effect relationships

explanation: Because descriptive studies don't involve testing or experiments, they can only tell you what is happening, not why it is strictly causing something else. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h7)

question: Why is detailed nursing documentation of a patient's nutrition care so important?

options.A: It guarantees the hospital gets zero complaints
options.B: It ensures continuity of care and creates a permanent record
options.C: It lets nurses prescribe their own diet orders
options.D: It replaces the need to give verbal shift handovers

explanation: Well done! Good charting keeps every nurse and team member on the same page across different shifts.

question: What is the primary function of carbohydrates in the human body?

options.A: Providing primary energy for daily activities
options.B: Producing essential hormones for growth
options.C: Regulating body temperature through sweating
options.D: Repairing damaged muscle tissues and organs

explanation: Carbohydrates are broken down into glucose, which serves as the body's main and most efficient energy source. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h1)

question: Why do doctors give epinephrine during a severe allergic reaction when airways close up?

options.A: It acts as a physiological antagonist to open airways through separate receptors
options.B: It permanently blocks the liver from making any more allergic cells
options.C: It chemically neutralizes the allergy antibodies in the bloodstream
options.D: It searches out and destroys histamine molecules directly inside the syringe

explanation: Epinephrine works through its own receptors to do the exact opposite of what the allergy is doing—relaxing the muscles and opening those airways right up!

question: What is the biggest cause of antimicrobial resistance today?

options.A: Misuse and overuse of antimicrobial drugs
options.B: Routine handwashing with antibacterial soap
options.C: Complete adherence to vaccination schedules
options.D: Strict adherence to sterile surgical techniques

explanation: Exactly right! Taking antibiotics when we don't need them—or not finishing the full dose—teaches germs how to survive our drugs.

question: Why does not drinking enough water put pregnant women at higher risk for urinary tract infections (UTIs)?

options.A: Faster bacterial growth caused by extra dietary fat
options.B: Reduced flushing of bacteria from the urinary tract
options.C: Increased production of sugary urine by the kidneys
options.D: Lower body temperature slowing down immune cells

explanation: Makes total sense, right? Drinking plenty of water means regular peeing, which naturally washes away nasty bacteria before they cause trouble.

question: How should a clinical instructor react if a student makes a mistake during a practice simulation?

options.A: Punish the student publicly to scare others
options.B: Kick the student out of the nursing program right away
options.C: Use the mistake as a teaching moment for reflection
options.D: Pretend nothing happened so nobody feels bad

explanation: Mistakes are normal when learning! A good tutor turns an error into a helpful lesson without making you feel bad about yourself.

question: When you are taking a family health history, which group of relatives should you focus on first?

options.A: Neighbors living in the same community
options.B: Colleagues and close personal friends
options.C: First-degree relatives like parents and siblings
options.D: Distant cousins and second-degree relatives

explanation: You nailed it! Parents, brothers, and sisters share the closest genetic traits with your patient, so their medical history matters most.

question: Why are informal sector workers in developing regions often at a higher risk for occupational lung disease?

options.A: Government laws completely ban safety masks in local factories
options.B: The tropical climate causes dust particles to become radioactive
options.C: They frequently lack proper personal protective equipment and health monitoring
options.D: Their lungs are naturally weaker than those of corporate office workers

explanation: The absence of safety gear, safety regulations, and routine medical checkups in informal industries greatly increases the risk of chronic lung injury. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why is it often so hard to enforce anti-FGM laws at the local community level?

options.A: Federal laws completely override all state and local police actions
options.B: Traditional rulers are legally permitted to bypass state courts
options.C: Medical doctors are required by law to perform the procedure instead
options.D: Cultural secrecy and fear of ostracization prevent people from reporting cases

explanation: That's right. Because FGM is deeply rooted in some cultures, families keep it a secret and are terrified of speaking out or reporting offenders.

question: What is the main advantage of teamwork between doctors, nurses, and dietitians in clinical nutrition?

options.A: Ensuring that the doctor makes all decisions without team input
options.B: Eliminating the need for nursing documentation on patient wards
options.C: Preventing gaps in care through shared expertise and communication
options.D: Reducing the number of working hours required for hospital staff

explanation: You got it! When healthcare professionals share their skills and communicate openly, patient care becomes much safer and more effective.

question: Why do nurses take a baseline set of vital signs when a patient is first admitted?

options.A: It gives a standard reference point to detect future clinical changes
options.B: It prevents the patient from developing hospital-acquired infections
options.C: It determines the exact medical diagnosis without needing lab tests
options.D: It fulfills the legal requirement to discharge the patient safely

explanation: Having an accurate starting measurement helps you immediately spot when your patient's condition starts getting worse. Great job thinking like a nurse! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h1)

question: Why do midwives frequently check if the uterus is firm after delivery?

options.A: To test the mother's abdominal muscle strength after labor
options.B: To ensure the uterine muscle is contracting well to prevent hemorrhage
options.C: To measure the exact amount of amniotic fluid left inside
options.D: To check if the baby is positioned correctly for feeding

explanation: Spot on! A firm, contracted uterus clamps down on blood vessels so the mum doesn't bleed too much.

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with heavy watery diarrhea and vomiting. What causes these intense symptoms?

options.A: Stomach acid production increases rapidly to destroy the liver
options.B: Infection causes complete destruction of the large intestine lining
options.C: A bacterial toxin forces massive water and electrolyte secretion into the gut
options.D: Inflammation blocks all blood flow to the kidneys

explanation: The cholera germ releases a toxin that tricks the gut into dumping lots of water and salts, leading to heavy fluid loss.

question: Why does a lack of financial transparency harm grassroots health committees?

options.A: It destroys community trust and discourages local donations and participation
options.B: It causes international pharmaceutical companies to raise drug prices
options.C: It forces health workers to close all clinics permanently
options.D: It automatically stops the federal government from paying nurse salaries

explanation: When villagers suspect mismanagement of local health funds, they lose faith in the committee and refuse to support health programs. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which specific cells are responsible for producing protective mucus in the intestinal lining?

options.A: Goblet cells
options.B: G-cells
options.C: Parietal cells
options.D: Chief cells

explanation: Goblet cells secrete mucus that coats the intestinal lining, shielding it from friction and corrosive digestive juices. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h6)

question: In drug supply and logistics, what does the term CIF stand for?

options.A: Cost, Insurance, and Freight
options.B: Client Invoice and Fee
options.C: Capital, Inventory, and Finance
options.D: Central Immunization Fund

explanation: CIF is just a handy shipping term! It covers the actual purchase price of imported drugs plus the cost of insurance and getting them safely delivered.

question: A patient on long-term steroid therapy asks why they need a medical alert bracelet. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: It proves to your insurance that you take your pills.
options.B: It warns people around you that you might gain weight.
options.C: It lets emergency staff know your adrenal glands are asleep if you have an accident.
options.D: It stops doctors from giving you new prescriptions.

explanation: Spot on! In an emergency, medical staff need to know your adrenal system is suppressed so they can provide extra steroid support your body can't make on its own.

question: Which of these is the best way to protect patient privacy during data collection?

options.A: Replacing patient names with code numbers on data sheets
options.B: Leaving interview notebooks open on the nurses' station desk
options.C: Posting study results on public bulletin boards in the ward
options.D: Sharing patient diagnoses with visiting family members

explanation: Well done! Using code numbers instead of real names hides patient identities and keeps their personal information safe.

question: How should controlled substances be stored in a residential care home?

options.A: In a secure double-lock system with strict inventory logs
options.B: In the kitchen refrigerator alongside resident food supplies
options.C: In an open cabinet in the nurses' station for quick access
options.D: Inside the resident's personal bedside drawer for self-administration

explanation: Well done! Because controlled drugs carry a high risk of misuse, they must always be double-locked and carefully tracked.

question: Why does the intestinal wall have a muscular layer (the muscularis)?

options.A: Secreting hormones into the bloodstream
options.B: Generating peristaltic waves to move contents
options.C: Filtering waste from local blood vessels
options.D: Absorbing digested sugars and amino acids

explanation: These muscles squeeze in a coordinated wave pattern (peristalsis) to push food smoothly along the digestive tract. You've got this!

question: Why might a baby in Gallows traction have trouble breathing deeply?

options.A: The ropes block fresh air from their face
options.B: The sticky tape gives off lung-irritating fumes
options.C: The heavy weights make the room air too thin
options.D: The elevated legs push up on the tummy and limit lung expansion

explanation: Lifting those legs straight up presses the tummy contents against the diaphragm, which can slightly crowd the lungs. Good catch for nursing assessments!

question: Which piece of information is most critical to document immediately during a patient's admission assessment?

options.A: Known drug allergies
options.B: Favorite television programs
options.C: Previous occupation history
options.D: Preferred clothing brand

explanation: Documenting allergies immediately prevents the accidental administration of medications that could cause severe or life-threatening reactions. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary when caring for a victim of breast ironing?

options.A: Hospitals require multiple signatures before prescribing simple painkillers
options.B: The patient needs medical, psychological, and social protection services
options.C: Physical wounds always heal faster when psychiatric drugs are given
options.D: Doctors are legally barred from treating burns without social workers

explanation: Recovery requires treating physical injuries, addressing emotional trauma, and ensuring long-term child safety. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h7)

question: Which group of professionals typically forms the core interprofessional team in an adult day care center?

options.A: Hospital administrators, accountants, and legal counsels
options.B: Nurses, social workers, activity coordinators, and therapists
options.C: Pharmacists, laboratory scientists, and radiologists
options.D: Surgeons, anesthetists, and operating room technicians

explanation: A multidisciplinary team combining nursing, social work, therapy, and recreation is standard for addressing holistic client needs. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h7)

question: A patient who lost both legs in a car accident last week is angry and crying over lost independence. How would you classify this response?

options.A: A mild seasonal mood shift
options.B: A normal childhood milestone
options.C: A congenital developmental delay
options.D: An acquired physical disability

explanation: Exactly. Sudden traumatic losses later in life bring heavy grief and shock as patients mourn the physical abilities they used to have.

question: What is one of the very early physical signs of pregnancy you might spot on a woman's breasts due to extra blood flow?

options.A: Shrinkage of the overall breast size
options.B: Complete absence of areolar pigmentation
options.C: Prominent and visible superficial veins
options.D: Active secretion of mature white milk

explanation: Because the body sends extra blood to the breasts to prepare for feeding, the veins near the surface become much easier to see. Neat physiological adaptation, right?

question: Why do children have different nutritional needs compared to adults?

options.A: Children require fewer calories per kilogram of body weight
options.B: Children do not need micronutrients until puberty begins
options.C: Adults have higher metabolic demands than growing children
options.D: Children are actively building new tissue and growing rapidly

explanation: Spot on! Growing kids need extra fuel and building blocks because their bones, muscles, and organs are developing fast. You've got this!

question: What is the best way for a nurse to care for an FGM survivor in the clinic?

options.A: Reporting the adult patient to local police immediately
options.B: Inspecting the surgical site without warning the patient
options.C: Refusing to discuss the cultural background of the practice
options.D: Using a trauma-informed and non-judgmental approach

explanation: Great choice! Trauma-informed care builds trust, lowers anxiety, and makes sure the patient feels safe and respected.

question: How should a nurse best respond when a palliative patient expresses deep anger about their illness?

options.A: Remind them that anger will only make their physical pain worse
options.B: Validate their feelings and provide a safe space to vent
options.C: Immediately leave the room to avoid confrontation
options.D: Tell the patient to remain positive for the sake of the family

explanation: Anger is a normal response to losing control and health; listening without judgment helps the patient process these heavy emotions. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h3)

question: What is the main issue in retrograde ejaculation?

options.A: Sperm cells fail to mature inside the epididymis
options.B: The testes produce zero fluid during the emission phase
options.C: Skeletal muscles contract too slowly to move semen
options.D: Semen flows backward into the urinary bladder

explanation: Spot on! When the bladder neck muscle fails to close properly, semen goes backward into the bladder instead of out.

question: Why can slouching lead to tummy troubles like heartburn or constipation?

options.A: It compresses the abdominal organs
options.B: It makes the liver swell in size
options.C: It speeds up intestinal transit too much
options.D: It stops the production of stomach acid

explanation: When you slouch, your upper body squeezes your tummy and intestines like a pinched pipe, which makes digestion a bit uncomfortable.

question: Why is keeping a strict fluid balance chart so vital for a Lassa fever patient?

options.A: To prevent both dehydration and dangerous fluid overload leading to pulmonary edema
options.B: To calculate the exact amount of oral medication required daily
options.C: To ensure the patient loses weight while admitted in the isolation ward
options.D: To test the concentration of protein present in the blood plasma

explanation: Because leaky blood vessels make fluid management tricky, too little fluid causes shock, while too much fills the lungs.

question: Which ethical principle are you upholding when you give a patient honest, complete details about a drug's side effects?

options.A: Maleficence
options.B: Paternalism
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Fidelity

explanation: Spot on! Autonomy is all about respecting the patient's right to make their own choices based on honest and clear information.

question: What is the very first thing that happens during the initiation stage of cancer development?

options.A: The tumor develops its own blood supply to grow
options.B: Promoting agents cause the mutated cells to multiply rapidly
options.C: Malignant cells travel through the blood to distant organs
options.D: A permanent mutation occurs in the cellular DNA

explanation: You got it! Initiation is step one, where a harmful agent (carcinogen) causes a permanent, irreversible change right inside the cell's DNA.

question: What is the main reason food holds such deep meaning in many religions?

options.A: Religious leaders mandate specific daily calorie requirements
options.B: It is closely tied to spiritual meanings, purity laws, and traditions
options.C: Diets were strictly designed to prevent infectious diseases
options.D: Ancient societies lacked basic knowledge of food preservation

explanation: Religious diets aren't just about nutrition science—they are deeply rooted in sacred commands, purity concepts, and passing down traditions through generations.

question: What is an important nursing task when dealing with different healthcare levels?

options.A: Setting the financial prices for private hospital medications
options.B: Guiding patients smoothly through appropriate referral pathways
options.C: Managing government tax allocations for public health centers
options.D: Issuing official operating licenses to traditional birth attendants

explanation: You're a star! Nurses use their knowledge of facility tiers to make sure patients get sent to the exact right place for their condition.

question: Which two theatre team members are primarily responsible for performing surgical counts?

options.A: Radiologic technologist and orderly
options.B: Surgeon and lead anesthesiologist
options.C: Patient and attending physician
options.D: Scrub nurse and circulating nurse

explanation: The scrub nurse and circulating nurse team up to carefully count and record all instruments, sponges, and needles used.

question: If you want to find out what a patient has eaten over the past 24 hours, what assessment tool do you use?

options.A: Biochemical lab panel review
options.B: Anthropometric measurement
options.C: Dietary history recall
options.D: Clinical physical examination

explanation: That's right! Asking a patient to recall everything they ate in the last day is a simple, effective dietary history check.

question: Why does taking strong, broad-spectrum antibiotics often lead to an annoying yeast infection?

options.A: It kills protective lactobacilli bacteria
options.B: It increases the production of vaginal glycogen
options.C: It lowers overall body temperature
options.D: It directly stimulates fungal spore production

explanation: Antibiotics are great, but they aren't picky—they wipe out our protective friendly bacteria right along with the bad ones, leaving yeast free to party! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h3)

question: Why do many patients hold back from talking to nurses about sexual health problems?

options.A: Lack of available medications
options.B: Embarrassment and cultural stigma
options.C: Mandatory insurance restrictions
options.D: Strict hospital visiting hours

explanation: It is completely normal for people to feel shy or worried about judgment when discussing intimate health. Creating a safe, open space as a nurse helps patients feel comfortable opening up!

question: How do cochlear implants work differently from standard hearing aids?

options.A: They only amplify sound in the outer ear
options.B: They are used exclusively for conductive loss
options.C: They require no external power source
options.D: They directly stimulate the auditory nerve

explanation: While regular hearing aids just make sounds louder, cochlear implants completely bypass damaged parts of the ear and zap electrical signals straight to the auditory nerve!

question: When a patient is put on a salt-free diet, what does it mainly cut out?

options.A: Table salt added during cooking or eating
options.B: Proteins found in red meat and poultry
options.C: Every single trace of sodium in fresh fruit
options.D: All water containing natural minerals

explanation: Great job! A salt-free diet simply means cutting out added table salt, not scrubbing away every natural trace of sodium in fresh foods.

question: A patient is admitted with sickle cell anemia. How is this genetic disorder typically inherited?

options.A: Y-linked paternal pattern
options.B: Autosomal recessive pattern
options.C: Trisomy anomaly pattern
options.D: X-linked dominant pattern

explanation: Sickle cell anemia is an autosomal recessive condition, meaning a child must inherit the abnormal gene from both parents to show symptoms. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why is it discouraged to use the word 'prove' in a research objective?

options.A: It makes the study take much longer to complete
options.B: A single study gathers evidence to test a hypothesis, rather than proving an absolute truth
options.C: The word 'prove' is grammatically incorrect in scientific writing
options.D: Ethics committees do not allow researchers to have strong opinions

explanation: Science builds knowledge brick by brick. A single study only gathers evidence to support or reject an idea—it rarely claims to 'prove' an absolute truth once and for all. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h7)

question: How many unique identifiers must you use to make sure you have the right patient?

options.A: Three completely different family members
options.B: Only one verbal confirmation
options.C: At least two unique identifiers
options.D: No identifiers if you already know them

explanation: Always check at least two things—like their name and hospital ID band—even if you know their face well. It's a quick habit that prevents big mix-ups!

question: Why is waist circumference often a better indicator of health risks than BMI?

options.A: It changes based on leg water retention
options.B: It is impossible for athletes to get a false reading
options.C: It requires expensive laboratory machines
options.D: It specifically measures fat stored around internal abdominal organs

explanation: Waist measurements target belly fat directly, showing the hidden visceral fat around vital organs that drives heart disease risk.

question: A patient with cancer is losing weight fast despite eating regular meals. What is a good first step to help them?

options.A: Reduce total daily protein intake to spare the kidneys
options.B: Initiate a strict low residue diet
options.C: Limit fluid intake during meal times
options.D: Switch to a high calorie, energy-dense meal plan

explanation: When the body's metabolic needs shoot up, boosting the energy density of food helps the patient stop losing weight and regain strength.

question: In tracheostomy care, what does the term 'decannulation' mean?

options.A: Permanent removal of the tracheostomy tube
options.B: Inserting a new mechanical ventilation machine
options.C: Inflating the cuff to maximum pressure
options.D: Cleaning the inner cannula with sterile water

explanation: Decannulation simply means the tube is finally and permanently removed because the patient no longer needs it. You're mastering the terminology!

question: Why do community nurses take their analyzed data back to the community for validation?

options.A: To hide negative health statistics from government officials
options.B: To punish local residents who refused to answer survey questions
options.C: To confirm the accuracy of findings with the community members
options.D: To print extra copies of the survey questionnaire

explanation: Validation is all about checking your homework with the people who live there to make sure your conclusions match their everyday reality.

question: What do non-profit and faith-based health organizations do with any extra money they make?

options.A: Reinvest them into their service mission
options.B: Use them to pay corporate luxury bonuses
options.C: Distribute them directly to private shareholders
options.D: Return them to federal tax authorities

explanation: Because they don't have shareholders taking home profits, any surplus goes right back into improving patient care and helping the community.

question: Why might a patient with high blood cell counts paradoxically face bleeding risks?

options.A: The body stops making fibrinogen completely
options.B: The excess platelets do not function right
options.C: Phlebotomy removes all clotting proteins
options.D: High blood pressure bursts skin capillaries

explanation: Even though platelet numbers look high, they are often faulty and don't do their clotting job properly, leading to bleeding worries.

question: Why do researchers measure participants before and after giving an intervention?

options.A: To measure the exact change caused by the treatment
options.B: To give patients something to do while waiting
options.C: To fill up extra space in the final research report
options.D: To prove that all patients had identical health scores

explanation: Baseline measurements show where the patient started, letting researchers calculate the exact difference the intervention made. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is the main difference between an additive interaction and a synergistic interaction?

options.A: Additive effects require three drugs, while synergistic effects only need two drugs
options.B: Synergistic effects are greater than the sum of separate effects, while additive effects equal the sum
options.C: Additive effects occur in the liver, while synergistic effects occur in the kidneys
options.D: Synergistic effects always cause dangerous toxicity, while additive effects are completely safe

explanation: Spot on! Additive is normal addition (1+1=2), while synergism is a multiplier effect where the total result punches above its weight class.

question: Which type of poultice is commonly used to retain heat for deep inflammation and boils?

options.A: Kaolin poultice
options.B: Salt crystal poultice
options.C: Dry cotton poultice
options.D: Ice water poultice

explanation: Kaolin is a heavy clay substance known for holding heat well to treat deep-seated swelling and boils. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is a constant physical challenge when nursing on a moving ship?

options.A: Frequent electrical storms inside underground tunnels
options.B: Exposure to extreme desert heat and blowing sand
options.C: Constant rolling, pitching, and vibrating of the vessel
options.D: Lack of oxygen due to high altitude mountain climbing

explanation: Exactly! The natural movement of the water means the ship is always moving, which makes doing clinical procedures a unique challenge.

question: Through which bone does smell nerve fibers pass to reach the brain?

options.A: Internal acoustic meatus of the temporal bone
options.B: Superior orbital fissure of the orbit
options.C: Cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone
options.D: Foramen magnum of the occipital bone

explanation: Spot on! Tiny nerve fibers pass upward through the tiny holes in the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone to reach the brain's olfactory bulb. Fun anatomy fact to keep in mind!

question: Why is teaching safe body mechanics to family caregivers such an important nursing duty?

options.A: It cures chronic illnesses in the patient.
options.B: It protects the patient from falls and the caregiver from back injuries.
options.C: It cuts down the monthly grocery bill.
options.D: It gets rid of the need for grab bars.

explanation: You nailed it! Good lifting habits keep both the helper's back safe and the patient secure during transfers.

question: What is the most effective way to improve community participation in rural immunization drives?

options.A: Relying solely on written posters placed inside clinic walls
options.B: Stopping all routine clinic visits to focus only on mass rallies
options.C: Engaging local community and religious leaders as advocates
options.D: Punishing parents who fail to bring their babies on time

explanation: Working with respected community and religious leaders helps build local trust and encourages families to accept and support immunization programs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h8)

question: A community nurse is preparing to measure a toddler's MUAC. Where on the arm should the tape be placed to find the correct midpoint?

options.A: At the thickest part of the bicep muscle
options.B: Right below the armpit crease
options.C: Directly over the middle of the forearm
options.D: Between the shoulder tip and the elbow tip

explanation: You've got this! To get an accurate MUAC, always locate the exact midpoint between the shoulder (acromion) and the elbow (olecranon).

question: What does 'test-retest reliability' check in a study?

options.A: Stability of scores over time
options.B: Agreement between two different observers
options.C: Equivalence of two different questionnaire versions
options.D: Internal similarity of survey questions

explanation: Spot on! Test-retest simply means giving the same test to the same people at two different times to see if the scores stay stable.

question: Why do home health nurses need to watch out for non-physical abuse just as much?

options.A: Emotional abuse always leaves visible marks on medical charts
options.B: Physical abuse never occurs without emotional coercion first
options.C: Coercion, control, and isolation are core dynamics of domestic abuse
options.D: Non-physical abuse is the only type reportable by law

explanation: You've got this! Abuse isn't only physical. Emotional and psychological control can trap and break a person just as deeply as physical blows.

question: What do we mainly mean by 'sewage' in public health?

options.A: Liquid waste from homes, businesses, and factories
options.B: Treated drinking water stored in community reservoirs
options.C: Industrial runoff containing only chemical fertilizers
options.D: Rainwater collected exclusively from street gutters

explanation: Think of sewage as the used, dirty water flowing away from residential houses, offices, and factories. It carries everyday waste and needs safe management to keep our communities healthy!

question: What is a major emotional and social challenge that HIV-positive mums often face regarding how they feed their babies?

options.A: Complete lack of interest in infant nutritional needs
options.B: Legal restrictions against breastfeeding in public places
options.C: Inability to find pediatric clinics in rural areas
options.D: Fear of stigma and disclosure within their communities

explanation: The fear of being judged or accidentally revealing their status to family and neighbors weighs heavily on many mums. Empathy goes a long way!

question: What is the main goal of birth preparedness and complication readiness (BPCR) during antenatal care?

options.A: To train family members to deliver the baby at home safely
options.B: To prevent dangerous delays in reaching emergency obstetric care
options.C: To remove the financial cost of hospital supplies completely
options.D: To guarantee that the baby is born on the exact estimated date

explanation: BPCR is all about planning ahead (transport, funds, blood donors) so that if an emergency strikes, the mother doesn't lose precious time.

question: What is the most common cause of trouble in the pituitary gland?

options.A: The body's immune system attacking the back part of the gland
options.B: Severe, long-term bacterial infections spreading through the brain
options.C: Cancerous tumors that have spread to the brain from the lungs
options.D: Benign (non-cancerous) tumors known as pituitary adenomas

explanation: Don't panic when you hear 'tumor'—most pituitary problems come from benign growths called adenomas. They can either pump out too many hormones or squish normal gland tissue.

question: How are sources arranged in an APA reference list?

options.A: Chronologically from oldest publication year to newest
options.B: Alphabetically by the first author's last name
options.C: Numerically in the order they appeared in the text
options.D: By the length of the journal article title

explanation: Spot on! Arranging them from A to Z by the author's last name makes finding sources super easy.

question: Which everyday task puts women in displacement camps at high risk of physical attack?

options.A: Receiving dry food rations directly from aid workers
options.B: Attending mandatory community health education workshops
options.C: Walking long distances alone to collect firewood and water
options.D: Participating in organized camp leadership meetings during the day

explanation: Going out to fetch water or firewood means walking through lonely, unlit areas far from help. It's a huge safety hazard for women in camps.

question: A patient with a broken leg complains of throbbing pain and winces when moving. Which option is a great nursing diagnosis focus?

options.A: Fracture of the right tibia and fibula bones
options.B: Prescription of narcotic pain medication
options.C: Surgical repair of the lower leg bones
options.D: Acute pain related to physical tissue trauma

explanation: Spot on! 'Acute pain' describes the patient's human response to their injury, which is exactly what we as nurses diagnose and manage.

question: What security practice involves giving staff access only to the patient files needed for their specific job duties?

options.A: Role-based access control
options.B: Universal computer sharing
options.C: Open public network browsing
options.D: Manual paper chart locking

explanation: Role-based access limits what parts of an EHR a user can see based on their specific job role, protecting patient privacy. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h7)

question: During a cholera outbreak, stagnant floodwater contaminating a community well represents which part of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Host
options.B: Agent
options.C: Environment
options.D: Immunity

explanation: Well done! The contaminated water is part of the environment—the external surrounding that allows the germ to reach people. You're mastering the basics!

question: Why do researchers use statistical tables alongside written text in a report?

options.A: Narrative text cannot contain numbers under any circumstance
options.B: Tables summarize precise values so the text can focus on main findings
options.C: Tables are meant to confuse readers who do not understand math
options.D: Tables are required by law for every medical document

explanation: Tables make heavy numbers easy to look at, which lets the written text focus on the most important patient care takeaways without getting cluttered.

question: Which group of people usually needs to visit the hospital or clinic the most?

options.A: Teens living in rural villages
options.B: Teenagers in secondary schools
options.C: Healthy young adults working jobs
options.D: Older adults and young children

explanation: Great thinking! The very young and our elderly grandparents have bodies that are more delicate against infections, so they tend to need healthcare services more frequently.

question: Why are new mums at higher risk for their bladder becoming too full after giving birth?

options.A: Complete blockage of the urethra by lochia
options.B: Permanent shrinkage of the urinary bladder
options.C: Excessive fluid intake forced by nurses
options.D: Decreased bladder sensitivity to pressure after birth

explanation: Spot on! Labor can temporarily numb the bladder, meaning the mum might not feel the urge to pee even when her bladder is quite full. That's why we always encourage regular trips to the restroom!

question: What does a higher needle gauge number actually mean?

options.A: A longer needle shaft
options.B: A duller needle tip
options.C: A thinner needle diameter
options.D: A larger medication volume

explanation: It can feel confusing at first, but remember: the higher the gauge number, the thinner the needle! You're learning fast.

question: A patient uses an electric oxygen concentrator and lives where power outages are common. What must be in their safety plan?

options.A: An agreement to rely solely on battery-operated kitchen fans
options.B: Advice to stop using oxygen completely whenever it rains outside
options.C: A plan to drive to the hospital emergency room every single night
